subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is meant by 'liturgical worship'?
options: Worship that follows a set structure, order and ritual
Worship carried out only in private at home
Worship with no words, prayers or music
Worship performed only by ordained priests
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a fixed order or liturgy, often the same each week, as in a Catholic Mass or Anglican service.

questions.q: Who first taught the Lord's Prayer to his followers?
questions.explain: The Lord's Prayer was given by Jesus to his disciples as a model for how to pray.

questions.q: How many sacraments does the Roman Catholic Church recognise?
questions.explain: Catholics recognise seven sacraments: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Reconciliation, Anointing of the Sick, Holy Orders and Matrimony.

questions.q: In which country is the Christian pilgrimage site of Lourdes?
questions.explain: Lourdes is in France, where Bernadette Soubirous reported visions of the Virgin Mary in 1858.

questions.q: The Eucharist commemorates which event in the life of Jesus?
questions.explain: The Eucharist recalls the Last Supper, when Jesus shared bread and wine with his disciples before his death.

questions.q: Which element is central to the sacrament of baptism?
questions.explain: Water is used in baptism as a symbol of cleansing from sin and new life in Christ.

questions.q: The pilgrimage community of Iona is located in which country?
questions.explain: Iona is a small island off the west coast of Scotland, home to an ecumenical Christian community.

questions.q: Which best describes non-liturgical worship?
options: Worship that does not follow a set form and can be more spontaneous
Worship that must always use the exact same words each week
questions.explain: Non-liturgical worship has no fixed order and may focus on Bible readings, preaching and spontaneous prayer.

questions.q: What does the Catholic belief in transubstantiation teach about the Eucharist?
options: The bread and wine become the actual body and blood of Christ
The bread and wine are only symbols and nothing changes
The bread and wine are shared only by priests
The bread and wine represent the disciples
questions.explain: Transubstantiation is the Catholic teaching that the substance of the bread and wine truly becomes the body and blood of Christ.

questions.q: Why do many Christians practise infant baptism?
options: To welcome the child into the Church family and remove original sin
Because babies can choose to follow Jesus for themselves
To replace the need for confirmation later in life
Because the Bible commands baptism only for infants
questions.explain: Infant baptism welcomes a baby into the Christian community and, in Catholic teaching, cleanses original sin, with parents and godparents making promises on the child's behalf.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a Christian going on pilgrimage?
options: To make a spiritual journey to a holy place to grow closer to God
To take a relaxing holiday away from religion
To earn money for their local church
To avoid attending normal Sunday worship
questions.explain: Pilgrimage is a journey to a site of religious significance undertaken to deepen faith, seek healing or show devotion.

questions.q: What does the season of Advent prepare Christians for?
options: The birth of Jesus at Christmas
The resurrection of Jesus at Easter
The coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
questions.explain: Advent is a season of preparation and expectation leading up to the celebration of Jesus' birth at Christmas.

questions.q: The season of Lent recalls which period in the life of Jesus?
options: The forty days he spent fasting in the wilderness
The three days he spent in the tomb
The forty days after his resurrection
The years he spent as a carpenter
questions.explain: Lent lasts forty days and reflects the time Jesus spent fasting and being tempted in the wilderness, and is often marked by self-discipline.

questions.q: What is meant by 'evangelism' in Christianity?
options: Spreading the Christian message and sharing the good news of Jesus
Building new cathedrals across the world
Collecting money for repairs to a church
questions.explain: Evangelism is the work of spreading the Gospel so that others may come to Christian faith, central to the Church's mission.

questions.q: During a service, worshippers sing spontaneously, raise their hands and speak in tongues, led by the movement of the Holy Spirit. This is best described as which form of worship?
questions.explain: Charismatic worship is spontaneous and emotional, emphasising the gifts and presence of the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: A Catholic privately confesses their sins to a priest, expresses sorrow and receives forgiveness and a penance. Which sacrament is this?
questions.explain: The sacrament of Reconciliation (Penance) involves confessing sins to a priest and receiving God's forgiveness.

questions.q: A Christian wishes to make a pilgrimage to the place traditionally associated with Jesus' death and resurrection. Where should they go?
questions.explain: Jerusalem contains sites linked to Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection, such as the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

questions.q: A church holds a festival celebrating the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the disciples fifty days after Easter. Which festival is this?
questions.explain: Pentecost celebrates the descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples and is often seen as the birthday of the Church.

questions.q: Which Christian festival celebrates the resurrection of Jesus from the dead?
questions.explain: Easter Sunday celebrates the resurrection of Jesus, the most important festival in the Christian year.

questions.q: Most Protestant churches recognise how many sacraments, and which are they?
questions.explain: Most Protestants accept only Baptism and the Eucharist as sacraments, since these were directly instituted by Jesus in the Gospels.
